quoteSelections.quote:
Additionally, ssr is defined similarly to asr but is restricted to speech signals, whereas asr targets general audio, including speech, music, and sound effects.
Fig. 2 illustrates the signal flow for the degradation and reconstruction processes of bwe and asr, where both waveforms and spectrograms are shown at each stage to visualize the signal transformations. Table 1 summarizes the key differences and commonalities between bwe, asr, and ssr. While bwe is defined by the restoration of spectral bandwidth, asr and ssr are characterized by temporal interpolation. Despite these differing definitions, all three tasks can be unified as ill-posed inverse problems—specifically spectral or temporal inpainting.

This section categorizes the literature by modeling paradigm, including ar, vae, gan, diffusion, flow, and bridge models, with representative approaches summarized in Table 3.

The model further incorporates a factorized magnitude-phase representation and sliding-window inference to support hr audio restoration at 44.144.1 kHz over long music segments.
7 Quantitative Analysis
To enable a fair and direct comparison across different asr/bwe paradigms, we re-evaluate representative discriminative, GAN-based, diffusion-based, and flow-based methods under a unified experimental setup. This quantitative analysis provides stronger empirical evidence for the trade-offs among reconstruction accuracy, perceptual quality, model complexity, and computational efficiency.
